From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: Audiencia, audiència, and audiência

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Spanish audiencia. Doublet of audience.

Pronunciation

[edit]

IPA(key): /aʊdiˈɛn(t)siə/, /ɔd-/, /-ˈɛnθiə/, /-ˈdjɛn-/

Noun

[edit]

audiencia (plural audiencias)

  1. (historical) An appellate court of the Spanish empire.
    • 1992, Edwin Williamson, The Penguin history of Latin America, London; New York: Penguin Books, →ISBN, page 21:
      After Cortés the government of New Spain degenerated under the rule of Nuño de Guzmán, president of the first audiencia, into a brutish exploitation of the Indians.

Synonyms

[edit]
  • audience

Hungarian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin audientia (“a hearing, listening”), from audire (“to hear”).[1] With -encia ending.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈɒudijɛnt͡sijɒ]
  • Hyphenation: au‧di‧en‧cia
  • Rhymes: -jɒ

Noun

[edit]

audiencia (plural audienciák)

  1. audience (a formal meeting with a state or religious dignitary)

Slovak

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /avdient͡sia/, [ˈau̯dient͡sia]
  • Rhymes: -ia
  • Hyphenation: au‧di‧en‧ci‧a

Noun

[edit]

audiencia f (relational adjective audienčný)

  1. audience

[edit]

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin audientia.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /auˈdjenθja/ [au̯ˈð̞jẽn̟.θja] (Equatorial Guinea, Spain)
  • IPA(key): /auˈdjensja/ [au̯ˈð̞jẽn.sja] (Latin America, Philippines)
  • Rhymes: -enθja (Equatorial Guinea, Spain)
  • Rhymes: -ensja (Latin America, Philippines)
  • Syllabification: au‧dien‧cia

Noun

[edit]

audiencia f (plural audiencias)

  1. audience
  2. a tribunal of justice of a defined territory which hears its problems, cases and lawsuits

Derived terms

[edit]
  • audiencia al rebelde
  • Audiencia Nacional
  • audiencia provincial
  • audiencia pública
  • audiencia territorial
  • índice de audiencia
  • sala de audiencia
  • tener audiencia

[edit]
